gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2's single 20 A solar input can only reach 1,000 W from a string working at 50 V or more under a 60 V ceiling (1,000 W ÷ 20 A = 50 V), while each EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus port needs only about 33 V for its 500 W (500 W ÷ 15 A).
standout_why: I compared against Volt & Valley's 'Best Power Station and Solar Panel Combo' (cited in both chats). It lists the DELTA 3 Plus as '2 MPPT, 500W each' and works out Wh/lb and $/Wh, but it gives no voltage or current window for any station, so it never shows the minimum string voltage. The BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 page ChatGPT cited gives 12V-60V and 20A Max separately but doesn't divide them. Our current page lists '1 input, 12–60 V, 20 A' and '2× XT60, 500 W each, 11–60 V, 15 A' but doesn't do the arithmetic either. None of these pages turns the limits into the 50–60 V operating window a shopper needs to reach 1,000 W on the BLUETTI.
decides: This supports the DELTA 3 Plus as the answer. The Elite 100 V2 also claims 1,000 W, but on one input it only gets there with a string operating between 50 and 60 V, a narrow window that common portable panels and series pairs can easily miss. Each DELTA 3 Plus port reaches its 500 W anywhere from about 33 V to 60 V, so two ordinary strings can fill it. Before landed losses, both stations take about 1.0 h at a full 1,000 W.

findings.label: Refill at full 1,000 W solar, using StorageReview's measured charge energy
findings.note: StorageReview measured 1,180 Wh to charge 0–100% (86.8% efficiency, on AC). 1,180 Wh ÷ 1,000 W = 1.18 h. Before losses: 1,024 ÷ 1,000 = 1.02 h. Solar-path losses may differ from AC.
